subject: Annual settlement mechanics, carry-forward credits, and ramp schedule for multi-year commitment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizondata.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.rao@horizondata.com, legal@horizondata.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify annual settlement and carry-forward mechanics for 3yr commitment

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week — team liked the throughput & cost forecasts. Before we pull procurement in, a few specific questions on the commercial mechanics for the 3-year advance commitment you proposed:

1) Annual settlement window — does unused prepay in year N roll forward into year N+1 as a credit, or is settlement strictly at the end of each contract year?

2) Buffer tolerance — we need a defined soft buffer (we call it a grace threshold) so short spikes don’t trigger immediate overage billing. Can you outline the percent thresholds and how overage tiers apply above them?

3) Ramp schedule / milestone discounts — we plan to ramp from 20% to 80% of committed capacity over 12 months. Are there milestone-based discount breakpoints tied to achieved throughput?

4) End-of-term settlement mechanics — for a 36-month deal, is there a single reconciliation at contract end, or annual reconciliations with a final true settlement? Also what documentation do you require from our side for audit/reconciliation?

Can you send a short note on each point and a draft clause we can share with legal?

Best,
Samir
Senior Procurement Manager
HorizonData

Attachment: horizon_usage_sample.csv (attachment referenced)

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@horizondata.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify annual settlement and carry-forward mechanics for 3yr commitment

Samir — thanks for the clear list. I’ve pulled finance and legal into the loop (Ben + Vanessa) and sketched answers below; attaching a short draft clause (draft-settlement-clause-v2.docx) and an updated pricing matrix for visibility.

High-level answers:
- Annual settlement & carry-forward: We support a one-year carry-forward of any unused annual commitment as a credit against the following year, capped at 25% of the following year’s committed units. Any remaining unused credits expire at the end of the second year.
- Buffer (grace threshold): Default soft buffer is 12% of annual commitment. Usage above that buffer but below 25% overage is billed at Tier 1 overage rate (discounted overage). Anything >25% above committed quantity in a year bills at standard overage rates.
- Ramp / milestone discounts: We can offer a step discount tied to quarterly ramp milestones: reach 40% of indexed committed tokens by Q2 = additional 3% discount on unit price for subsequent quarters; reach 70% by Q4 = extra 5% discount, cumulative. These are subject to verification by our usage telemetry.
- End-of-term settlement: We do annual reconciliations at each anniversary plus a final contract-end settlement. Annual carry-forward credits (per rule above) apply; final shortfalls or excess usage are resolved at contract end with the standard overage prices. We require monthly usage reports (CSV export + signed summary) for audit; Redwood will provide our telemetry export and audit logs.

Next steps: I’ll send a redline to the draft clause by tomorrow. If HorizonData prefers no carry-forward, we can remove that but would need higher upfront pricing or a smaller term discount.

Regards,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft-settlement-clause-v2.docx; redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Suggested concession bounds for HorizonData (RDW-24578)

Team — quick notes before we go back to Samir/Legal. I’m fine with the one-year carry-forward but recommend tightening the cap to 20% (not 25%) unless Horizon compensates with a smaller term discount. Rationale: carry-forward increases bookkeeping exposure and reduces realized revenue if they underconsume year 2.

Buffer: 10-12% soft buffer is acceptable. If they want a lower buffer we should escalate to Finance for a reduced per-unit price.

Ramp discounts: Agree with quarterly checks, but suggest making milestone verification explicit: auto metrics + a 7-day dispute window for the customer to raise anomalies. Also add a clause that discounts apply only to committed unit pricing (not to metered overage).

Final settlement: require our standard telemetry export + customer-signed usage summary. If Horizon requests a third-party audit option, add a cost-recovery clause (customer pays auditor).

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify annual settlement and carry-forward mechanics for 3yr commitment

Hi Samir — adding a legal lens here and proposing contract language extracts you can give to your counsel. Key edits included:

1) Carry-forward credit clause (proposed extract): "At each annual anniversary, any unused portion of Customer's Annual Committed Units may be carried forward to the following contract year as a one-time credit, provided such carry-forward does not exceed twenty percent (20%) of the following year's Annual Committed Units. Any carry-forward balance not utilized by the end of the following contract year shall expire and shall not be refundable."

2) Buffer / overage tiers (proposed extract): "A soft buffer of ten percent (10%) of Annual Committed Units applies. Usage in excess of the buffer and up to twenty-five percent (25%) above the Annual Committed Units shall be billed at the Tier 1 Overage Rate. Usage exceeding twenty-five percent (25%) above the Annual Committed Units in any contract year shall be billed at the Standard Overage Rate. Redwood may apply graduated tiers for multi-month sustained over-usage as detailed in the pricing matrix."

3) Verification & audit: "Redwood will provide a monthly usage export. Customer shall submit a signed usage summary within thirty (30) days of each anniversary to raise any disputes. Disputes must include supporting evidence and are subject to a seven (7) day review window. If a third-party audit is requested, Customer shall be responsible for audit fees unless material discrepancies (>5%) are found in Redwood's favor."

Samir — happy to set up a quick call between our legal teams if they want to redline these clauses directly.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft-settlement-clause-v2.docx (redline), redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx

Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify annual settlement and carry-forward mechanics for 3yr commitment

Vanessa / Chloe — thanks for the clear options and the redline. A couple of quick asks from HorizonData Legal:

- Can the carry-forward cap be 25% instead of 20%? They argue it’s needed for our projected ramp variability. We understand Redwood's revenue exposure; can you propose a halfway concession (22.5%) or a size-based exception (25% in year 1 only)?
- We’d like the buffer to be calendar-month smoothed (rolling 30-day average) rather than absolute annual percent for spike protection. Is that feasible operationally?
- Regarding audit fees: can you agree that if an audit finds a discrepancy >3% in Redwood's favor, Redwood absorbs fees; otherwise Horizon pays?

If we can get a drafted compromise clause reflecting these items, we’ll run it quickly through procurement and legal and aim to execute next week. Sending procurement contact offline.

Best,
Priya Rao
Head of Procurement, HorizonData
